Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid are lifelines for millions—but decades of DC mismanagement have pushed these programs toward insolvency. The SSA’s new identity verification rules are a start to curb fraud, but real reform requires slashing bureaucratic bloat. Medicare Advantage overpayments drain billions annually, while Medicaid’s structural flaws invite waste.

The answer isn’t just more funding—it’s auditing every dollar, cutting middlemen, and redirecting savings to beneficiaries. Protect the programs by purging inefficiency, not expanding broken systems.

Taxpayers deserve accountability, not empty promises.

The real issue isn’t Trump or Republicans—it’s the bloated healthcare bureaucracy that drives up costs. The ACA’s endless subsidies are a band-aid on a system riddled with administrative waste, hospital price-gouging, and Big Pharma profiteering. Minnesota’s own reinsurance program (MPSP) proves states can stabilize markets WITHOUT federal overreach.

Instead of blaming policies, let’s audit where the money actually goes: $190B in annual Medicare fraud, $150B in hospital upcharging, and bureaucrats skimming 25% of every healthcare dollar.

Cut the middlemen, not the care.

The real crisis is a bloated Medicaid system riddled with waste and fraud—something the One Big Beautiful Bill finally addresses. Democrats want to keep funneling billions into bureaucratic black holes while hospitals inflate prices and taxpayers foot the bill. This shutdown threat? Pure theater.

The House passed a clean funding extension; Senate Democrats blocked it to protect their failed Obamacare subsidies. Restoring accountability isn’t a “healthcare crisis”—it’s fiscal sanity.

Cut the waste, fund what works, and stop holding government operations hostage to bail out broken systems.
